hints.title: Square only after checking signs
hints.body: Put t=a2≥0. Both sides of |x2−t|=t|x−1| are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the equation.
hints.recap: The parameter appears only through t, and the case <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> needs attention.
hints.pitfall: Squaring an arbitrary signed equality is not always reversible, but here it is.
hints.pause: Factor the difference of the two squared sides.

recall.reminder: Squaring is reversible when both compared expressions are known nonnegative.

hints.title: Investigate the factored equation
hints.body: The squared equation factors as x(x−t)(x2+tx−2t)=0. First investigate the zero-parameter case. For a positive parameter, calculate the quadratic discriminant and use its coefficients to investigate the signs of its roots before combining them with the linear-factor roots.
hints.recap: Root existence, root signs and coincidences all affect the number of distinct solutions.
hints.pitfall: Count distinct values and check whether any factors share a root.
hints.pause: Determine the roots in the zero-parameter case, classify the quadratic roots for a positive parameter and compare them with the roots of the linear factors.

recall.reminder: Product roots form a union, with shared roots counted once.

hints.title: Test possible overlaps
hints.body: For a positive parameter, test each root from a linear factor in the quadratic factor. Its constant term helps with the zero root; substitute the other candidate and solve the resulting parameter condition. Keep the zero-parameter case separate.
hints.recap: A shared root reduces the number of distinct solutions, so count the exceptional parameter separately.
hints.pitfall: The question asks for the smallest impossible count, not the largest attainable count.
hints.pause: Derive every overlap condition, verify its parameter range, count distinct roots in all cases and identify the smallest unavailable count.

recall.reminder: Root counts change at parameter values producing shared or repeated roots.

solution:
Let t=a2≥0. Since both sides are nonnegative, squaring gives an equivalent equation: (x2−t)2=t2(x−1)2. Its difference of squares factors as [x2−t−t(x−1)][x2−t+t(x−1)]=x(x−t)(x2+tx−2t)=0.

For t=0, only x=0 occurs. For t>0, the quadratic has two distinct real roots of opposite signs, since its product is −2t<0. Neither is zero. Its positive root coincides with x=t precisely when 2t(t−1)=0, hence at t=1.

Thus there are three distinct roots at t=1, four at other positive t, and one at t=0. These are all possible counts. The smallest unavailable value is 2.

Answer B: n=2.
knowledgePattern: Factor the squared absolute-value equation and track coincident roots
